description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

# Apple HIG: Integrate a capability into the product task

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the product benefit and capability prerequisites before entering the technology-specific procedure. Avoid adding a system integration solely to decorate an existing flow.
2. Define consent/account/capability availability and the meaningful result, cancel, failure and recovery paths applicable to that integration. Keep sensitive information and system ownership clear.
3. Preserve supplied branding, hardware and platform qualifications. HIG states experience expectations; verify current APIs against implementation documentation when writing framework-specific code.
4. Deliver an integration contract or correction in the existing stack, with source-supported choices, fallbacks and evidence limits. Do not claim a payment, health, spatial or connected-device runtime test from a static specimen.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

# Apple HIG: Perception, meaning and adaptable presentation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the actual barrier or design decision: readability, visual hierarchy, imagery meaning, movement, locale, privacy or spatial placement. Choose the corresponding topic procedure rather than loading every foundation.
2. For text access, combine Typography with Accessibility only where size, reflow or reading alternatives matter. Use VoiceOver when grouping, semantics or navigation needs a procedure of its own.
3. For color/material decisions, separate content hierarchy from controls and evaluate the actual appearance/background/settings context. Preserve semantic meaning when appearance changes.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the person’s primary task and the target platform before translating a screen. Read that platform’s procedure; use Principles to resolve hierarchy and Designing for games only for gameplay.
2. Compare navigation, window/scene model, primary input, attention duration and state restoration. Preserve the product task while changing the interaction appropriate to the destination platform.

name: apple-hig-designing-for-ios
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting an iPhone experience for handheld touch, interrupted use, orientation changes, and system entrypoints.
---

# Make the iPhone task usable in the hand

Read [Designing for iOS](../../references/designing-for-ios.md). Inspect the current task, its entry and return points, supported orientations, input, and any supplied implementation. Distinguish a brief check from extended work. For a review, anchor problems to supplied screens/behavior; for design or adaptation, revise the requested artifact in its existing stack.

Choose what must remain immediately visible during the task. A brief check needs its result and primary action close together; extended editing can expose additional controls without crowding the initial screen. Put frequent touch actions within comfortable reach, generally toward the middle/lower display, while preserving system navigation and swipe-back behavior. Move secondary commands into a short discoverable path rather than shrinking every control to fit.

Trace interruption and resumption: preserve the selected item, draft, or playback context when another app takes focus. Specify portrait/landscape and enlarged-text rearrangements without inventing a new navigation hierarchy for each orientation. Use touch and onscreen keyboard as the baseline, then offer appropriate voice or accessory paths. Add location, biometric, payment, or motion features only when their benefit reduces task effort and access is appropriate.

For repeated out-of-app actions, choose a relevant system entrypoint and a precise destination: a quick action starts an action, search opens the found content, and a widget exposes a useful glance. Do not add every entrypoint to every app.

**Before → decision → after:** A parcel app opens a dense desktop-style table and requires opening three menus to find the latest delivery. A handheld glance needs delivery state first. The revised home screen shows the active parcel and “Show pickup code,” keeps history one step away, and returns a widget tap to that parcel rather than a generic home screen.

Deliver a revised screen/flow or implementation plus interruption, orientation, and text-size acceptance checks. Fail if the primary action becomes unreachable, Back conflicts with a custom gesture, or resuming loses work. Screenshot review cannot establish touch comfort or actual system integration; state pending device checks.

For detailed adaptation use [Layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md); for custom touch gestures use [Gestures](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-gestures/SKILL.md); for a chosen glance use [Widgets](../../../apple-hig-system-experiences/.topics/apple-hig-widgets/SKILL.md).

name: apple-hig-wallet
description: Use when designing or reviewing Wallet passes, field/semantic-tag hierarchy, add/view/update lifecycle, order tracking, or contextual Wallet identity verification.
---

# Put the useful credential or order state into the right Wallet model

Read [Wallet](../../references/wallet.md). Inspect whether the task concerns a pass, order, or identity request; identify platform/device, existing data/assets, and design/review/adaptation scope. Preserve the PassKit/order integration and verify current API/service availability. A pass appearing on Watch does not imply every Wallet verification flow works there.

For passes, choose the style by actual purpose and put essential information in fields/semantic tags, not embedded artwork or device-vulnerable layouts. Keep collapsed headers meaningful and fronts uncluttered; back/supplemental detail serves less frequent needs. Use the guide's image specifications and system barcode APIs, preserving essential content through phone/Watch crop differences. Poster/semantic styles need tags plus appropriate older-system fallback fields.

Offer system addition after the relevant purchase/registration, retain Add for absent/removed passes and View in Wallet for existing ones, and stop repeated suggestions after refusal. Keep expiry/relevance/voiding and changing details accurate. Deletion needs permission; interruptive updates are for time-critical changes, not marketing.

For orders, supply data promptly even while pending and maintain actual shipping/pickup fulfillments, final confirmed price, management/support links, and useful receipt data. Use detailed delivery states only with supporting carrier data; avoid duplicate notifications. For identity, request minimum necessary attributes in transaction context with retention intent/duration, supported system controls, and another method when unavailable. In-person reading belongs to ID Verifier.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a concert pass puts the seat number only in a background image, repeats Add prompts after refusal, and sends promotional “changed” alerts. Decision: the credential must remain readable across devices and updates must serve the event. After, seat/time live in appropriate fields/tags, existing passes open through View in Wallet, declined suggestions stop, and alerts are reserved for a meaningful time-critical event change.

Deliver the chosen model's field/lifecycle/update contract and corrected artifact. Fail if essential information vanishes on Watch, order status exceeds known evidence, or identity requests exceed the task. File/schema checks do not prove Wallet rendering, pass delivery, carrier updates, or encrypted identity handling; identify supported-runtime checks.

Use [Apple Pay](../apple-hig-apple-pay/SKILL.md) for payment and [ID Verifier](../apple-hig-id-verifier/SKILL.md) for in-person mobile-ID reading.

---
name: apple-hig-privacy
description: Use when designing or reviewing permission timing, purpose strings, pre-permission explanations, tracking requests, data minimization, or private platform inputs.
---

# Ask for precise access when its purpose is clear

Read [Privacy](../../references/privacy.md). Inspect the feature's actual data needs, transfers, storage, current permission flow, and supported platform. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Produce the requested copy/flow/data-handling changes in the existing stack; distinguish documented platform restrictions from additional application recommendations.

Map each requested category to a specific feature and minimum necessary scope. Remove collection without a concrete benefit; prefer on-device work where it avoids unnecessary transfer. Explain collection/use accurately and flag App Store disclosure updates needed when behavior changes. Respect private email and tracking choices rather than designing around them.

Ask when the person invokes the feature. Launch-time requests need an essential, obvious dependency. Write a short active purpose sentence explaining use and reason. If context is sufficient, omit a custom pre-alert; if explanation is essential, use one clear continuation to the real system alert without imitating Allow/Don't Allow. Keep the guide's special pre-alert restrictions distinct from ordinary onboarding. Tracking requires its system authorization before collection and must not be incentivized or manipulated.

Choose one-time location access for suitable individual tasks using the system location button on supported platforms; preserve permitted customization and all localized/accessibility-sized text. Protect secrets with established authentication/keychain mechanisms. For Mac, account for sandboxing/distribution and fast user switching. For visionOS, separate system rendering assistance from permission-gated Full Space ARKit data; gaze remains private, and imported phone-camera assumptions may need removal or content import.

**Before → decision → after:** A bird journal asks for contacts, microphone, and continuous location at launch although only “Attach current location” uses location. Decision: request only the specific action's needed access. After, journaling works immediately; the attachment action offers the supported location control, and its purpose explains adding the sighting's location.

Deliver a data-purpose/access matrix and corrected permission sequence/copy or implementation. Fail if collection precedes required consent, copy obscures the real use, or unrelated work is gated on optional access. Report code/flow evidence separately from actual authorization prompts and privacy-setting behavior; this procedure does not certify security or legal compliance.

Use [Sign in with Apple](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-sign-in-with-apple/SKILL.md) for that authentication choice and [Augmented reality](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-augmented-reality/SKILL.md) when room/camera access is essential.

For health-related work, finish the domain decisions as well as the permission
sequence. Read [CareKit](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-carekit/SKILL.md)
for care plans, scheduled treatment tasks, or symptom/event recording;
[HealthKit](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-healthkit/SKILL.md)
for health-data access and sharing; and
[ResearchKit](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-researchkit/SKILL.md)
for study participation and research consent. These experience procedures help
choose task, data, and consent behavior in the existing stack; consulting a
framework-named topic does not require adopting that SDK. General privacy,
language, and accessibility guidance alone does not resolve those domain choices.

# Designing for iOS Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. An iPhone experience must work both during brief checks on the move and through extended games, browsing, or media sessions. People switch among apps frequently. ## Best practices - Design for a medium-sized, dense display viewed at roughly 1–2 feet, usually held in one or both hands. Accommodate portrait and landscape use. - Keep primary content and actions clear, with secondary operations reachable through a small number of interactions rather than many simultaneous controls. - Support touch gestures, onscreen keyboards, and voice; use motion sensors, nearby spatial interactions, or personal information only where they improve the task. - Put frequent touch controls within comfortable reach, commonly the middle or lower display. Preserve swipe-back navigation and list-row gestures. - Adapt to orientation, Dark Mode, and Dynamic Type without breaking context. - With permission, use platform data and services to reduce typing: location, biometric authentication, and payments are examples. - Integrate appropriate system entry points: widgets, Home Screen quick actions, Spotlight search, Shortcuts, and activity views. Their familiar behavior helps people act outside the main app. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here.

# Wallet Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/wallet) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. ## Contents - [Passes](#Passes) - [Pass anatomy](#Pass-anatomy) - [Designing passes](#Designing-passes) - [Pass styles](#Pass-styles) - [Pass images](#Pass-images) - [Order tracking](#Order-tracking) - [Identity verification](#Identity-verification) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) - [Resources](#Resources) - [Change log](#Change-log) Wallet stores cards, IDs, passes, and keys on phone/Watch and supports payments, identity, and order tracking. Use PassKit/system interfaces to keep these exchanges familiar and trusted. ## Passes Offer system one-tap addition after a relevant purchase/registration; for predictable repeat additions, request one-time background-add permission. The system notifies additions. A custom preview may include the Add to Apple Wallet button. Suggest externally created passes on the next app visit, but stop after refusal. Add related passes together and bundle web downloads. Keep an Add button available for absent/removed passes and a direct View in Wallet link for existing ones. Set expiry/relevance/voiding accurately, obtain deletion permission, and supply time/location metadata for Lock Screen or supported Live Activity suggestions. Update changing details, but reserve interruptive change messages for time-critical fields, never marketing or minor support-detail edits. ## Pass anatomy Fields specify visible information; semantic tags explain content to the system for suggestions and featured actions. Poster event and semantic boarding styles require tags and should also include fallback fields for older iOS. Supplemental sheets can link from the front; the back contains infrequently used legal/settings detail. ### Pass field types Logo/name and header remain visible when collapsed. Primary fields convey the most important content, secondary/auxiliary fields useful supporting information, footer fields categories such as membership type, and back fields additional details. Exact arrangement depends on style. ## Designing passes Use Pass Designer templates or a blank canvas and create a clean digital pass rather than copying paper. Test phone/Watch variations and never put essential information solely in imagery/fields that disappear on another device. Keep fronts uncluttered, collapsed headers informative, brands recognizable, text well contrasted over art, and language device-independent. Do not pad image assets because Watch can crop whitespace. ## Pass styles ### Boarding passes Use for specific journeys/transit with origin/destination. Airlines use semantic tags; other transit types use fields. ### Coupons Use for offers and discounts. ### Event tickets Use for individual events or season access. Poster styles can use full-art backgrounds/semantics; nonposter styles use standard fields and can add background/thumbnail art. ### Store cards Use for loyalty, points, discounts, and gift cards, showing a balance where relevant. ### Poster generic passes Use a full-background layout for flexible cases outside other categories. ### Generic passes Use for remaining needs such as gym membership or coat-check claims. ## Pass images Supply efficient PNG assets at @2x/@3x. Keep information as accessible fields/tags rather than embedded text, and add barcodes through APIs/Pass Designer instead of baking them into images. Always provide an icon. ### Logo For nonsemantic airline/non-airline boarding, coupon, nonposter event, generic, and store passes: `logo.png`, 50–160 pt wide × 50 pt high, at top-leading. Avoid inner shadows that reduce readability. ### Primary logo For semantic airline, poster event, and poster generic passes: `primaryLogo.png`, 30–126 pt wide × 30 pt high, at top-leading. ### Secondary logo For a poster event’s additional issuer/organizer: `secondaryLogo.png`, 12–135 pt wide × 12 pt high, at bottom-trailing. ### Icon All pass styles use `icon.png`, 38 × 38 pt; supply square corners for system rounding. ### Strip image Coupon/store `strip.png` is 375 × 144 pt. Keep text-background regions quiet and high contrast, put key art toward bottom/trailing, and do not embed text. ### Thumbnail Event/generic `thumbnail.png` is 60–90 pt wide × 90 pt high. Use rounded artwork and transparent PNG. ### Background Nonposter event `background.png` is 343 × 503 pt. Poster event/generic `artwork.png` is 358 × 448 pt. Keep content within safe areas, allowing for a material strip at the bottom and any barcode; preview in Pass Designer. ### Footer Airline boarding `footer.png` is 268 × 15 pt. ## Order tracking Supply WalletOrders data immediately after purchase even while payment/fulfillment is pending, then keep status and shipping/pickup details current. Apple Pay can add order details automatically; from iOS 17, Track with Apple Wallet can appear on confirmation/status/tracking pages or email. Re-adding an existing order opens it. Provide opaque 300 × 300 px PNG/JPEG logo and distinct product images with simple solid backgrounds. Keep localized descriptions concise and the price equal to the confirmed final amount. ### Displaying order and fulfillment details Include a universal order-management link, clear per-item name/price/image data, all items at order level and only relevant ones per fulfillment, and optional transaction PDF receipts. Supply associated app IDs in priority order: link to the highest-priority app installed on the device, or to the first listed app when none are installed. Avoid duplicate app/Wallet notifications. Provide at least a merchant website plus useful phone/email/support/Messages contacts. Support multiple shipping or pickup fulfillments with ETA, carrier tracking link/number, needed pickup barcode, and clear instructions. Keep fulfillment UI focused on tracking. Name the carrier only when known, otherwise retain the generic tracking label. Use detailed onTheWay/outForDelivery/delivered states only with supporting carrier data, otherwise shipped; provide a tracking link when available. Explain Issue/Canceled directly with cause and remedy. ## Identity verification From iOS 16 on iPhone, apps/Clips can request ID attributes from Wallet in context. Apple does not create/view the ID documents; the app receives encrypted data unreadable on-device. For in-person reader use, follow ID Verifier instead. Offer verification only when supported and provide another method otherwise. Ask exactly when the transaction needs it, explain use through a concise active complete sentence with punctuation, and request only necessary fields such as an age threshold. For example, an account-opening identity check can explain that legally required identification helps prevent fraud; a rental driving-privilege check can explain that local law requires a valid right to drive. Specify retention intention/duration using system APIs so the sheet explains it. Choose Verify Age/Verify Identity when that finishes the transaction, Continue when more non-Wallet data is still required, or Verify with Apple Wallet when those labels do not fit and verification finishes the flow. Labels have automatic multiline variants. Use the system black button with white text, optional light outline against dark surfaces, and matching corner radius. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS/macOS/visionOS rules; tvOS is unsupported. ### watchOS Passes appear in a scrolling carousel even without a Watch-specific app. Tapping reveals extra information in a scrollable details view, including overflow from the main layout. Every style can show different image/field subsets. Watch always crops strip art to the card’s aspect ratio and may remove whitespace from other images, so keep essential content out of vulnerable areas. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/wallet) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 8, 2026, January 17, 2025, December 18, 2024, September 12, 2023, February 20, 2023, November 30, 2022, September 14, 2022.

# Privacy Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Communicate collection and usage clearly and protect granted data. Keep App Store privacy disclosures accurate for new releases and updates; people rely on them before downloading. ## Best practices Collect only what the specific feature requires and make access as precise as possible. Respect Hide My Email, Mail Privacy Protection, and tracking choices. Prefer on-device processing, including Create ML/Neural Engine where useful, to avoid unnecessary server transfers. Use system encryption, key management, and established security protections, including CloudKit’s additional encrypted data types where available. ## Requesting permission Protected categories include personal/location/health/financial/contact information, user-created content, messages/calendar/music/gameplay/HomeKit data, media, Bluetooth/Wi-Fi/local network resources, camera/microphone, the advertising identifier, and permission-gated ARKit data in a visionOS Full Space. The system displays the app’s purpose string and stores choices/descriptions in privacy settings. Ask when the person invokes the relevant feature. Request at launch only when access is essential and obviously necessary, such as location for navigation or room information for a spatial game that needs walls. Write a short, specific, active, complete sentence in sentence case with a period, explaining both use and reason. Vague promises of a better experience and commands to enable access do not explain the need. ### Pre-alert screens, windows, or views Usually context explains the request. If extra explanation is essential, use one button clearly leading to the system alert, such as Continue/Next; do not label it Allow or mimic the actual consent choice. Do not add cancellation, close, or other actions except those needed for legal consent. These restrictions apply to pre-permission custom explanations, not ordinary unrelated onboarding screens. ### Tracking requests Show the AppTrackingTransparency alert before collecting tracking information, including if tracking begins at launch. Do not offer incentives, imitate a permission prompt, display an image of the alert, annotate behind it, or otherwise manipulate rushed choices. Such patterns can cause App Review rejection. A legally required consent view before/after the system alert is permitted by the source’s stated review guidance. ## Location button On iOS/iPadOS/watchOS, the system location button provides one-time access at the task’s moment of need. The first tap teaches and confirms its behavior through a system alert; later taps grant access without repeating that education. Authorization expires when app use ends. With no prior status it resembles Allow Once; an existing While Using status is unchanged. Use it for individual tasks such as attaching a location or finding a nearby item/store. Customize only the supplied title, filled/outline glyph, foreground/background colors, and corner radius. Keep all localized and accessibility-size text untruncated and maintain contrast/transparency limits. Persistent customization violations can prevent location access even though the button still triggers other app actions. ## Protecting data Prefer passkeys; if passwords remain, add two-factor verification. Use Face ID, Optic ID, or Touch ID to protect continued signed-in access where appropriate. Store secrets in the encrypted keychain, never plaintext files even with restrictive permissions. Prefer established authentication, Sign in with Apple, and Password AutoFill over invented schemes. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS/tvOS/watchOS rules are listed. ### macOS Sign externally distributed apps with a valid Developer ID. Use sandboxing to limit resource/data access; Mac App Store apps require it. Account for fast user switching rather than assuming the current person is the only signed-in account. ### visionOS System ARKit algorithms support lighting, mapping, persistence, segmentation, and related rendering in Shared Space without exposing raw data to apps. ARKit API access requires Full Space, and plane estimation, scene reconstruction, image anchoring, and hand tracking require permission. Gaze remains private: system hover feedback can respond before a tap without disclosing where someone looks. Compatibility back-camera input is blank; front-camera input represents spatial Personas with permission. Adapt imported phone/tablet camera-dependent features by removal or content import instead of assuming conventional camera capture. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 21, 2023.

item.text: The brief identifies five problems: an image-based barcode, hidden event details, a marketing destination, incorrect cancellation status, and unnecessary identity exposure. I’ll specify a native event pass with structured fields, a direct ticket destination, and an explicit cancellation lifecycle. Update delivery and scanner behavior will remain pending validation.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > interface.md <<'EOF'
# Venue ticket pass — revised specification

Platform: iPhone Wallet (iOS). Task: identify the event, find the venue and present the correct admission credential during a brief check at the gate. Use a native PassKit event-ticket pass, with standard nonposter fields; do not build a simulated Wallet screen. Wallet owns pass layout, barcode presentation and system controls. Minimum OS/API support must be verified during implementation; no SDK availability is established by this specification.

## Field and destination contract

| Surface | Required content |
| --- | --- |
| Logo/name | Recognizable venue or issuer name; provide an icon. Branding must not carry essential ticket text. |
| Collapsed header | Event date and explicit status: “Valid”, “Canceled”, or “Expired”. |
| Primary | Event title. |
| Secondary | Event start date/time with venue time zone, and venue name. |
| Auxiliary | Gate and section/row/seat when assigned; use “General admission” when applicable. |
| Details/back | Full venue address, doors time if known, admission instructions, ticket reference, support contact and “Ticket details” link. Retain date/location on the front; details supplement them. |
| Barcode | Generate using system barcode facilities from the issuer's current admission token. Never embed a screenshot or a barcode in decorative artwork; no user editing/uploading of the credential. |

Bind fields to canonical event/ticket data, using stable field identifiers for updates. Do not invent unknown gates, seats or doors times. Include event time/location relevance metadata; supplying venue coordinates does not require collecting the person's location. Keep essential information in fields rather than images, including when a pass also appears on Watch. Inspect Watch overflow/cropping before release; iPhone scope does not establish Watch rendering success.

“Ticket details” opens the exact event and ticket in the installed app through a supported link, with an HTTPS equivalent when the app is unavailable. It shows admission status, venue/address, directions destination, and cancellation/refund information when relevant. It never opens the marketing home page. Authenticate only when needed for private management actions; preserve the ticket destination through sign-in and app interruption. Use opaque identifiers in links, with no embedded identity data or admission token. An unavailable ticket shows “Ticket unavailable” with retry/support, not a generic landing page. Do not place invented custom buttons inside the Wallet pass.

## Credential and lifecycle contract

- After confirmed purchase/registration, offer the system Add to Apple Wallet flow. Canceling addition leaves the ticket available in the app. Stop unsolicited repeat suggestions after refusal; keep a deliberate Add action available for absent or removed passes. For an existing pass, expose View in Wallet. Do not duplicate a ticket on re-add.
- The issuer is authoritative for token validity and event state. Replace the screenshot with a machine-readable credential, not a promise of screenshot resistance. Use an opaque token without personal details; scanner-side validation must reject revoked/canceled credentials. Token format, refresh and offline scanner policy require implementation verification.
- Active ticket: show “Valid” only when the issuer considers admission valid. Encode event times with a time zone and format visible dates for the user's locale. Persist the selected ticket across interruption; keep the saved pass usable without opening a marketing website.
- Changed date, time, venue or gate: update the same pass and relevance metadata from the issuer. Use an interruptive change message only when the change is time-critical; never for advertising or a minor support edit.
- Canceled event: revoke admission at the issuer, update the same pass to “Canceled”, apply supported voiding metadata, and stop presenting a usable admission barcode in the delivered canceled pass. Retain event name/date/venue for recognition. Details say “This event is canceled. This ticket cannot be used for entry.” Link to this ticket's actual refund/support state; do not promise an unconfirmed refund. A cancellation merits a time-critical change message.
- Expired ticket: set accurate expiration metadata and show “Expired”; it must not remain labeled Valid. Do not delete a canceled or expired pass without permission.
- Delivery failure/offline: retain the last received pass, retry delivery when connectivity returns, and show the last confirmed state plus update time on the app's ticket page. An issuer cancellation cannot instantly change an offline Wallet copy. The admission system must reject the canceled token even if a stale pass still says Valid. Do not describe a queued update as delivered.

## Data minimization

| Data | Purpose and handling |
| --- | --- |
| Event, venue, seat/gate, status | Needed for admission and wayfinding; expose as structured pass fields. |
| Opaque ticket reference/token | Needed for support/validation; token contains no identity attributes and is treated as a credential. |
| Full name, birth date, home address, email, phone, government ID details | Not needed by this supplied admission task. Omit from front, back, barcode payload, artwork, URLs and change messages; adding to Wallet must not newly collect these. |

No camera, contacts, tracking or user-location permission is required to add or show this ticket. No Wallet identity-verification flow is introduced. If a future venue requires identity verification, specify its actual purpose, minimum attributes and alternative process separately; do not print identity data on this pass. Review disclosures if actual data handling changes.

## Release acceptance contract

1. Inspect a generated pass: event-ticket style, structured title/date/time/venue/seat fields, meaningful collapsed header, icon and system barcode configuration; no screenshot credential or unnecessary identity data in any payload or asset.
2. On supported iPhones, add/cancel/refuse/remove/re-add/view the same ticket. Verify system UI, no duplicates or repeated unsolicited prompts, and preserved destination after interruption/sign-in.
3. Test a specific ticket link with and without the app, signed in/out, and unavailable ticket data. Each resolves to that ticket or its explicit recovery state, never marketing.
4. Exercise valid → changed → canceled and valid → expired. Check issuer rejection of revoked tokens, visible status, voiding/expiry metadata, relevance metadata, truthful refund copy and notification policy. Test delayed delivery and offline phone/scanner cases separately; do not accept stale Valid as proof of admission.
5. Inspect actual iPhone layouts in supported orientations, enlarged text and long localized date/venue/seat values. Confirm essential fields remain discoverable without image text or layout overlap. Inspect the resulting Watch pass if distributed there. Verify the barcode on venue scanners; static field inspection is insufficient.

## Guidance basis

Source-backed choices: [Wallet — Passes](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/wallet#Passes), [Pass anatomy](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/wallet#Pass-anatomy), [Designing passes](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/wallet#Designing-passes), [Event tickets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/wallet#Event-tickets), and [Pass images](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/wallet#Pass-images) support the native model, field hierarchy, lifecycle and barcode correction. [Privacy — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy#Best-practices) supports minimum data use. [Designing for iOS — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios#Best-practices) supports a focused glance and preserved context.

Exact field allocation, ticket routing, status copy, issuer/scanner revocation and recovery behavior above are concrete product decisions, not quoted universal HIG requirements. Links identify the official source of the supplied local guidance; no online verification was performed.
EOF"

# Result

Patched "'`interface.md` in place from the one-sentence brief into a concrete iPhone Wallet event-ticket specification. It replaces the mutable barcode screenshot with a system-generated credential, exposes event date/time/venue in structured fields, routes to the exact ticket, defines cancellation/expiration/update behavior, and removes unnecessary identity details from all pass surfaces and payloads.

## Decisions

- Use a standard nonposter event-ticket pass. This matches venue admission and avoids artwork-dependent essential information. Wallet owns rendering; API support remains to be verified.
- Keep event identity and admission status visible, with seat/gate and useful details behind them. Add/View, refusal, removal and re-add now have explicit behavior.
- Treat cancellation as both credential revocation and a pass update. Preserve the canceled ticket for recognition and support, rather than deleting it. Offline delivery can leave stale UI; scanner enforcement is a separate requirement.
- Remove identity data rather than moving it to the back. An opaque credential is still sensitive and does not by itself prevent screenshot reuse.
- Exact ticket routing, field placement, recovery copy and scanner policy are proposed product requirements. They extend the supplied HIG guidance; they are not asserted Apple API guarantees.

Official source links and their material recommendations are included in `interface.md`, using only the installed local snapshot.

## Worked before/after

Illustrative fixture, not supplied production event data: “Harbor Lights”, November 14, 2026, 7:30 PM America/New_York, Harbor Hall, Gate B, Section 102 / Row C / Seat 8.

Before: a mutable barcode screenshot; no visible event date/location; opening details goes to marketing; after cancellation it still says Valid; unnecessary identity details are printed.

After, while active: primary “Harbor Lights”; header date and “Valid”; structured start time with venue time zone and “Harbor Hall”; assigned gate/seat; system barcode from an opaque issuer token. Ticket details opens this ticket'"'s app/web destination. No birth date, address, email or ID data appears in pass content.

After issuer cancellation: revoke the token, deliver an update for the same pass showing “Canceled” and supported voiding metadata, remove its usable admission barcode, retain event context, and show “This event is canceled. This ticket cannot be used for entry.” The ticket destination supplies confirmed refund/support information. If the phone is offline, its old pass may remain visible; the issuer/scanner must reject the canceled token. The specification does not promise instantaneous Wallet updates.

## Acceptance evidence

Passed — static specification inspection:

- All five supplied defects have explicit corrections in the edited artifact.
- Field hierarchy, precise destination/fallback, addition/refusal/re-add, cancellation/expiry, delayed update recovery and data-purpose handling are specified.
- Release checks cover payloads/assets, device layout, interruption, links, state transitions, notification policy, offline behavior and scanner validation.

Failed — original brief against the revised contract: screenshot credential, hidden event information, generic marketing route, canceled-as-Valid status and unnecessary identity exposure. These are reported brief defects, not independently reproduced runtime failures.

Not executed — pass generation/signing/schema validation, SDK compilation/API availability, Wallet addition/rendering or update delivery, iPhone/Watch layout, localization/text-size execution, VoiceOver or other accessibility execution, deep-link/authentication execution, barcode scanning, offline scanner enforcement and security testing.
